claims.text: After the backend is disabled, the frontend and query type schema still advertise the 'sql' expression type — is that acceptable?
Docstring coverage is 25.00% which is insufficient - the required threshold is 80.00%. Functions are missing docstrings.
(*DB).TablesList has no call sites and shares its name with the package-level sql.TablesList.
Several methods such as NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands and db.QueryFramesInto return 'not implemented'.
DuckDB has been removed from the tree, but comments, the feature toggle description, and frontend copy still mention DuckDB.
enableSqlExpressions: the name promises something the function doesn't do, and it uses an inverted boolean name.
No test pins down the new 'SQL expressions are disabled' behavior.
The enableSqlExpressions function has flawed logic that always returns false, effectively disabling SQL expressions unconditionally:
Is this disablement permanent, or will it be re-enabled via the sqlExpressions toggle once a replacement SQL engine lands?
Is the trimming of go.mod / go.sum / go.work.sum actually clean when a real build is run?

The enableSqlExpressions security check only guards the ReadQuery code path used when FlagExpressionParser is enabled, but in default configuration buildCMDNode calls UnmarshalSQLCommand directly for TypeSQL, completely bypassing this check - the security gate should be added to the TypeSQL case in buildCMDNode or within UnmarshalSQLCommand
